<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { FileUpload, FormField, type Upload } from '@weft/ui'

// Each file is sent as it is added, with its progress; removing it while it uploads cancels it.
const files = ref<File[]>([])
const upload: Upload = (file, { signal, onProgress }) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest()
    xhr.open('POST', '/api/files')
    xhr.upload.onprogress = (e) => e.lengthComputable && onProgress(e.loaded / e.total)
    xhr.onload = () => (xhr.status < 300 ? resolve(xhr.response) : reject(new Error(xhr.statusText)))
    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Network error'))
    signal.addEventListener('abort', () => xhr.abort())
    const body = new FormData()
    body.append('file', file)
    xhr.send(body)
  })
</script>

<template>
  <FormField label="Receipts">
    <FileUpload v-model="files" multiple :upload="upload" />
  </FormField>
</template>

components.name: Form
components.purpose: A form that checks its values against a Weft field schema before it submits.
components.use: For any form whose values need checking before they are sent, with the same rules the server enforces.
components.avoid: For a search box or a single setting that takes effect at once, a Form is not needed.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the fields inside it adapt.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; its fields stack in a column.

props.name: state
props.description: The values, by field name: an object the fields bind into with `v-model`.

props.name: schema
props.description: The rules each field must meet, by name: `{ email: { required: true, email: true } }`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in it, buttons too, and a submit does nothing.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: as disabled, and `aria-busy`, so a second submit does nothing.

props.name: loadingAuto
props.description: Busy on its own while the submit handler's promise is pending.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Bound with `@submit`: runs once every field is valid, with a copy of the values; a promise it returns keeps the form busy.

emits.name: error
emits.description: Submitted with errors: each failing field's sentence, by name.

components.notes:
`state` is the values, an object the fields bind into with `v-model`;
`schema` is a Weft field schema - plain JSON a server can send, the same
shape the Go contract will generate - keyed by field name:

    { email: { required: true, email: true }, age: { min: 18, message: 'You must be 18 or over.' } }

Each rule is optional: `required`, `min` and `max` (a length for text and
lists, bounds for numbers), `pattern` (matched against the whole text, as the
HTML attribute does), `email`, `url` (an absolute `http:` or `https:`
address with a host: "Enter a web address that starts with http:// or
https://."), `enum` (a list of the values allowed: "Choose one of: a, b."),
and `message` in place of the default sentences. `required` counts text of
only spaces as empty; every other rule skips only a missing or empty value
(`undefined`, `null`, `''` or an empty list), so spaces alone fail `enum`,
`url` and `email`. Its TypeScript type is `FieldSchema`, and
`validateFields` checks values against one anywhere.

**When it checks.** On submit every field is checked. With errors, `error`
fires with them, each FormField with a matching `name` shows its error, and
focus moves to the first invalid control; without, the `@submit` handler
runs with a deep copy of the values (lists and objects too), typed as
`state` is. After the first submit, a field is checked again when it is
left, and a field showing an error is checked as it changes, so the error
goes the moment it is fixed - but no new error appears while typing.

**Server errors.** A template ref's `setErrors({ email: 'That address is
taken.' })` shows errors from elsewhere. Leaving such a field keeps its error
(the server said so, and nothing changed); changing the field checks it
again. `validate()` checks without submitting, and `clear()` clears every
error.

A server error on a field the schema has no rule for clears the first time
that field changes: there is nothing to check it against.

**Its template ref.** `FormApi` is the ref's type:
`useTemplateRef<FormApi>('form')` gives `setErrors(errors)`, `validate()`,
`clear()`, `submit()` (as the submit button would), and `errors` and
`loading` read as values.

**Disabled.** The content sits in a `<fieldset>` with no frame, so
`disabled` disables every control in the form at once - Weft's and native
ones, Buttons included - and a submit does nothing. A fieldset leaves links
alone, so a Link, or a Button with `to`, in the form reads it and is
disabled as a disabled link is: no address, `aria-disabled`, no navigation.

**Busy.** `loading`, or with `loading-auto` (on by default) a `@submit`
handler that returns a promise, makes the form busy until it settles: it sets
`aria-busy`, a second press or Enter submits nothing, its fields are
disabled and its links have no address. The submit button is not natively
disabled, so it keeps focus: it shows its spinner, is `aria-busy` and
`aria-disabled`, and ignores presses. Any other button works, so a Cancel or
Stop can abort the submit (as in Nuxt UI). Raw native controls in the form (a
plain `<input>` or `<button>`) are not blocked while busy, only while
`disabled`; use Weft's components to have them follow the form. A field that
had focus (Enter pressed in it, or focused as `loading` turned on) gets it
back when the form is done. (`@submit` is a handler prop, as in Nuxt UI, so
the form can wait for it.) The native form has `novalidate`: Weft shows the
errors, not the browser.

**Before it is live.** A Form sends only through its `@submit` handler,
so it belongs in an island: one drawn by the page, with no island around
it, is never live and does nothing on submit. Until its island is live it
sends nothing: a small inline script at the top of the page's `<head>`
stops every submit of a Weft form from the first moment, and the form is
`method="post"`, so with scripts off its own submit puts nothing in the
address (a submit button the app gives `formmethod="get"` still does).
Its fields stay usable meanwhile: what a person types, or a password
manager fills, before the island is live is kept when it hydrates and
reaches the model. An app's own `form.submit()` fires no submit event, by
the platform's design, so it bypasses the script and sends a POST to the
page.

A site with a Content-Security-Policy must allow the page's inline
pre-paint script, `<script data-weft-prepaint>`, by its hash or with
`'unsafe-inline'` (a nonce needs a server that writes one into each answer,
which a built page does not have). The Form's part of it is exactly

    window.addEventListener("submit",function(e){var t=e.target;if(t&&t.classList&&t.classList.contains("weft-form"))e.preventDefault()},true)

and a page whose other components register pre-paint code too (AppShell
with `persist`, a closable Banner with an `id`) has it joined into the same
script, one snippet a line, so the hash depends on the page's components.

components.name: FormField
components.purpose: The label, description, hint, error and required marker around one form control.
components.use: Around every form control that needs a visible label, inside a Form or not.
components.avoid: For a Checkbox or Switch whose own label says everything, the control alone is enough.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the control inside it adapts.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; it fills the width of its container.

props.name: label
props.description: What the control is for. The label slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: Help in a sentence, under the label ("We never share it."). The description slot replaces it.

props.name: hint
props.description: A short note beside the label ("Optional", "3 of 10"). The hint slot replaces it.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong, under the control; `true` marks it invalid without a sentence. Wins over the Form's error.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required (an asterisk, and aria-required on the control); a Form's schema can say so too.

props.name: name
props.description: The field's name: the control's name, and the key of its value, rules and error in a Form.

props.name: id
props.description: The control's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`, for the label and the control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control.

components.notes:
The label sits over the control and is `for` it: the control takes the
field's id (set `id` to choose it). A control that is not a labelable element
- a RadioGroup, a CheckboxGroup, a Slider - is named through
`aria-labelledby` instead, and the label then has no `for` (on the server
the label keeps it until the island hydrates, as the control's setup runs
after the label is written). A range Slider names each thumb by the label and
its own end: "Price Minimum".

`description` is a sentence under the label; `hint` is a short note beside
it ("Optional", "3 of 10"); `error` sits under the control. All three
describe the control through `aria-describedby`, in that order, and an
error marks it `aria-invalid`. `error: true` marks it invalid without a
sentence (or with the `error` slot). `required` draws an asterisk, hidden
from assistive technology, and sets `aria-required` on the control. The
default slot receives `{ error }`, for a control drawn by hand.

**In a Form,** `name` links the field to the Form: it shows the Form's error
for that name, it is required when the schema says so, and leaving or
changing the control lets the Form check it again. An `error` given to the
field wins over the Form's.

A width left out falls back to the nearest smaller one given, else to the

components.name: Header
components.purpose: The bar at the top of a page: the site's name, its navigation and actions.
components.use: At the top of a site's pages (a landing page, docs); an app built on AppShell has its header there.
components.avoid: Inside a card or a dialog, use their own header slots; for an app frame with a sidebar, use AppShell.

adapts.input: The narrow menu button is at least --weft-hit-min square on touch (Button's rule).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: When the viewport is narrow and a menu slot is given, the middle gives way to a menu button that opens the menu in a Sheet from the start side.

props.name: title
props.description: The site's or app's name, shown at the start as a link to `to`. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: to
props.description: Where the title links.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: The menu button's name, and the sheet's title.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Stick to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls.

props.name: open
props.description: The narrow menu open or shut, bound with `v-model:open`.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: The narrow menu opened or shut.

components.notes:
The `title` links to `to` (`/`); the `leading` slot replaces it with a logo.
The default slot is the middle (a NavigationMenu), `actions` the end. The
`menu` slot is what a narrow screen shows in its sheet, with `close()` to
shut it after a link is chosen; bind the sheet with `v-model:open`. Without
a `menu` slot the middle stays when narrow, and a NavigationMenu there takes
its own narrow form. `sticky` (on) keeps it at the top while the page
scrolls.

Before mounting both the middle and the menu button render, and CSS shows
the menu button on a narrow viewport (`max-width: 639.98px`) when there is a
menu; once mounted `data-layout` says `compact` or `full` and only that
form's part renders. When it changes, the sheet closes, and focus in the
part that goes moves to the menu button, or to the middle's first link.

It is a `<header>`: the page's banner landmark when it is not inside an
article, aside, main, nav or section.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A Lucide icon by name, drawn as an inline SVG in the current text colour.
components.use: Wherever an icon helps recognition, beside a label or, with a label of its own, standing alone; Weft components take the same names in their icon prop.
components.avoid: For pictures and logos, use an img; never let an icon alone carry meaning without a label.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an icon is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the surrounding text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: name
props.description: The Lucide icon's name, as on lucide.dev: `trash`, `chevron-down`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the icon is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What the icon means, for an icon that stands alone; without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

components.notes:
Names are Lucide's, as listed on lucide.dev/icons: `trash`, `chevron-down`.
Only the icons a build uses ship: the build finds static names in templates
(`name="trash"`, `icon="plus"`) and `icon: '…'` properties in scripts, and
fails with a sentence naming the file for a name Lucide does not have. Names
made at run time go in the `icons` option of `weftIcons()`.

Without `label` the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); with one it is
an image with that accessible name (`role="img"`). `size` is `sm` (16 px),
`md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it the icon is 1.25em.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: A one-line text field in a box that can hold an icon, a unit or a button before and after the text.
components.use: For a short answer typed in full - a name, an email address, a search - bound with v-model, usually inside a FormField.
components.avoid: For text over several lines, use Textarea; for a number stepped up and down, use InputNumber; for a choice from a known list, use a select or RadioGroup.

adapts.input: An md input is max(--weft-control-md, --weft-hit-min) tall, so 44 px on touch, the same height as an md Button beside it; sm and lg keep their sizes, and a pseudo-element behind the field grows the hit area to 44 px.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; put it in a Grid or a FieldGroup to share a row.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The text, bound with `v-model`; a number with `v-model.number` or `type="number"`.

props.name: type
props.description: The native input type: `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `tel`, `url`, `number`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points here.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the text. The trailing slot replaces it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (a lookup as it is typed): a spinner after the text, and `aria-busy`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not editable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`, for a form the browser checks.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The text changed (on each key, or on change with `.lazy`).

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The input lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The input took focus.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change: the text was committed.

components.notes:
Bind the text with `v-model`; `v-model.trim`, `.number` and `.lazy` work as
on a native input (`type="number"` also gives a number, or `null` when it is
empty). Attributes such as `placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode` and
`aria-label` go to the `<input>`; `class` and `style` go to the box.

**Leading and trailing.** `icon` and `trailing-icon` draw Lucide icons, hidden
from assistive technology; the `leading` and `trailing` slots replace them
with anything (a unit, a clear button). A press on the box outside the text
focuses the text; a button in the box keeps its own press.

**Loading** puts a spinner after the text and sets `aria-busy`; the field
stays editable (a lookup runs as it is typed).

**In a FormField** the input takes the field's id (so the label points to
it), its name, `aria-describedby` (the description, the hint and the error; an
`aria-describedby` of its own comes first), `aria-invalid` and
`aria-required`. In a FieldGroup it takes the group's size.

**For other components:** a template ref's `focus()` focuses the text, and
`input` is the element; Select, Combobox and DatePicker build on this box.

components.name: InputNumber
components.purpose: A number typed or stepped up and down, kept between a minimum and a maximum.
components.use: For a quantity, a count or an amount where a step up or down is natural.
components.avoid: For a value picked along a range, use Slider; for numbers that are really codes (a phone number, a card), use Input.

adapts.input: md is 44 px tall on touch, as an md Button is, and the steppers become large buttons, 44 px wide (28 px on pointer) and at least 44 px tall through their hit areas.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The number, bound with `v-model`; null when it is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The number to start with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: min
props.description: The smallest it may be.

props.name: max
props.description: The largest it may be.

props.name: step
props.description: How much a step (an arrow key or a stepper) changes it.

props.name: wheel
props.description: Change it with the mouse wheel while it has focus. Off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: decrementLabel
props.description: The decrease button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: incrementLabel
props.description: The increase button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled, steppers too.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not changeable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The number changed: stepped, or typed and committed.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The input lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The input took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the number with `v-model`; it is `null` when the field is empty.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern): Up and Down step by `step`,
Page Up and Page Down by ten steps, Home and End go to `min` and `max`.
Typed text is read when it is committed - Enter, or leaving the field - and
kept within `min` and `max`; text that is not a number goes back to the
value. Stepping by decimals leaves no floating-point dust (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3).

**Mouse wheel:** off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.
With `wheel`, the wheel steps it, but only while it has focus.

**Steppers:** out of the tab order (the keys do their work), named by
`decrement-label` and `increment-label` ("Decrease", "Increase"), disabled at
the bounds, and a press keeps focus where it was. The input is a text input
with `role="spinbutton"` and `inputmode="decimal"`, carrying
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.

components.name: InputTags
components.purpose: A text field that turns what is typed into tags, each with a ×, for a list of short free values.
components.use: For keywords, email addresses, labels: values typed rather than chosen from a list, several of them.
components.avoid: When the values come from a known list, use Combobox with multiple; for one value, Input.

adapts.input: The field is at least max(--weft-control-md, --weft-hit-min) tall, so 44 px on touch, and each × has a hit area of at least --weft-hit-min.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its container's width and grows taller as tags wrap onto more lines.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The tags, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tags it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the empty field.

props.name: delimiter
props.description: Typing this adds the text before it as a tag; a string or a pattern.

props.name: addOnPaste
props.description: A paste goes in at the caret, and the whole text, split at the delimiter, becomes tags.

props.name: addOnTab
props.description: Tab adds the text as a tag (and stays).

props.name: addOnBlur
props.description: Leaving the field adds the text as a tag.

props.name: duplicate
props.description: The same tag may be added twice.

props.name: max
props.description: At most this many tags.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: At most this many characters in a tag.

props.name: convertValue
props.description: Turn the typed text into the tag's value.

props.name: displayValue
props.description: The text a tag shows for its value.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the tags. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: a spinner at the end, and aria-busy.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Tags cannot be added or taken out.

props.name: required
props.description: At least one tag is required: aria-required on the field (not the native `required`, which would read the draft).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its tags submit under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The text field's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The tags changed.

emits.name: addTag
emits.description: A tag was added, with its value.

emits.name: removeTag
emits.description: A tag was taken out, with its value.

emits.name: invalid
emits.description: A tag was refused (a duplicate, or past `max`), with its value.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The tags changed by an addition or a removal.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: Focus left the field and its tags.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The field took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the tags with `v-model` (an array). Enter adds the typed text, trimmed,
as a tag (and does not submit the form; Enter in an empty field does), and
so does typing the `delimiter` (a comma; a pattern works). With
`add-on-paste` a paste goes in at the caret and the whole text, split at the
delimiter, becomes tags (a draft and a pasted word together are one tag);
`add-on-tab` adds on Tab, `add-on-blur` when focus leaves. A duplicate is
refused unless `duplicate`, and so is a tag past `max`: both emit `invalid`
and the text stays. `convert-value` turns the text
into the tag's value and `display-value` the value into the tag's text.

The tags are a list (`role="list"`) before the text, each a list item with a
× button named "Remove …", outside the tab order. Backspace in the empty
field, or ArrowLeft at its start (ArrowRight right to left), moves focus onto
the last tag; the arrows move between tags and back to the field; Backspace
or Delete takes out the focused tag, focus going to its neighbour or the
field. Inside a FormField the text field takes the field's id, description,
error and required mark; with a `name` (or its FormField's) the tags submit
in hidden inputs, one each. `required` sets `aria-required` (no native
`required`, which would read the draft). `disabled` blocks typing and
removing. The `item-label` slot draws a tag's text (`{ item, index }`), as
Combobox's does an option's; its old name `item-text` still works and is
deprecated.

components.name: InputTime
components.purpose: A time of day, typed part by part in the locale's order and hour cycle.
components.use: For a time in a form - an opening hour, a meeting's start, an alarm - bound as HH:mm.
components.avoid: For a duration, use InputNumber; for a date, DatePicker.

adapts.input: On pointer it is a group of spinbuttons, one per part of the time, each a tab stop, keyed and typed into. On touch it is the platform's time field, whose own picker the phone draws (a wheel or a clock), with the same min, max and step, 44 px tall; it shows the time in the phone's own format. The input can change while it has focus; the time stays and focus moves to the other form's first part.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container, as Input does.

props.name: modelValue
props.type: string | { readonly hour: number; readonly minute: number; readonly second?: number } | { start: TimeInput | null end: TimeInput | null } | null
props.description: The time, bound with `v-model`: `HH:mm` (`HH:mm:ss` with granularity second), or a Time with `value-format="object"`; null while a part is empty. With `range`, `{ start, end }`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.type: string | { readonly hour: number; readonly minute: number; readonly second?: number } | { start: TimeInput | null end: TimeInput | null } | null
props.description: The time it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: range
props.description: Two times, a start and an end, bound as `{ start, end }`; an end before the start is marked invalid.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: `iso`: bound as an `HH:mm` string. `object`: as a `Time`.

props.name: granularity
props.description: The smallest part shown: `hour`, `minute` or `second`.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description: 12 or 24-hour time; the locale's when not set.

props.name: step
props.type: { hour?: number; minute?: number; second?: number }
props.description: How far Up and Down step each part.

props.name: min
props.type: string | { readonly hour: number; readonly minute: number; readonly second?: number }
props.description: The earliest time allowed; an earlier one is marked invalid.

props.name: max
props.type: string | { readonly hour: number; readonly minute: number; readonly second?: number }
props.description: The latest time allowed; a later one is marked invalid.

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale of the order, digits and AM/PM; a WeftProvider's applies when not set, else en-US.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the time. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: nothing can be focused or changed.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not editable.

props.name: required
props.description: A time is required (aria-required; native `required` on touch).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its time submits under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The group's id (the field's on touch); inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says, to translate them.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The time changed: `HH:mm`, a Time, `{ start, end }` with range, or null.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The time was changed by a key or by the platform's picker.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: Focus left the time.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The time took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the time with `v-model`: `HH:mm` (`HH:mm:ss` with `granularity="second"`,
`HH:00` with `hour`), or a `Time` of `@internationalized/date` with
`value-format="object"`; it is null until every part is filled. With a `name`
it submits that string in a hidden input.

On pointer the parts follow the locale (`1:05 PM` in en-US, `13:05` in en-GB,
`오후 1:05` in ko-KR); `hour-cycle` (12 or 24) overrides its hour cycle. Each
part is a `spinbutton` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`,
`aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`, named "Hour", "Minute", "Second" and
"AM/PM" (`labels` translates them); the group has `role="group"`, named by
its FormField's label (`aria-labelledby`, the label losing `for`, since a
group is no form control) and described by its hint and error.

**Keyboard.** Up and Down step the part (by `step`, wrapping round), Home and
End go to its ends, digits type into it (in the locale's digits too; the
next part takes focus once this one is full, or once no further digit could
follow), A and P (or the locale's words' first letters) set AM and PM,
Backspace clears a digit, then the part, Left and Right move between parts
(mirrored right to left), and a separator typed moves on.

With `range` it is two times, a start and an end, bound as `{ start, end }`
(each null while empty; null when both are) and submitted as `name[start]`
and `name[end]`: on pointer two groups of parts, named "Start time" and "End
time", Left and Right going on from one to the other; on touch two platform
fields so named. An end before the start is marked invalid.

A time before `min` or after `max` is marked invalid (`aria-invalid`,
`data-invalid`) but still bound, as a native time field does. `disabled`
takes the parts out of the tab order; `readonly` keeps them focusable and
unchanged. The `leading` slot (or `icon`) draws the box's start.

components.name: Island
components.purpose: Renders a component on the server and makes it interactive in the browser, on load, when idle, when visible or when a media query matches.
components.use: For the few interactive parts of an otherwise static page, a counter, a form, a menu, so only they ship JavaScript.
components.avoid: For content that never changes in the browser, render the component directly; a page with no island ships no script at all.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the island's component adapts as it would anywhere.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: when
props.description: When the browser hydrates it: at `load`, when `idle`, when `visible`, or when `media` matches.

props.name: media
props.description: The media query for `when="media"`, such as `(min-width: 1024px)`.

props.name: component
props.description: The `<script setup>` SFC to render and hydrate; its file name is the island's id.

props.name: props
props.description: Props for the component, sent to the browser as JSON.

components.notes:
The component must be a `<script setup>` single-file component: its file name
is the island's id. `props` travel to the browser as JSON, so they may hold
only strings, finite numbers, booleans, null, arrays and plain objects; the
build refuses anything else with a sentence naming the prop, `-0` (which
JSON writes as `0`), a symbol key and an array's members other than its
items (which JSON leaves out) included. `when="media"`
needs a `media` query. Ids from `useId` inside an island are counted per
island, so they match between the server and the browser.

Ids are counted by the island's position among the page's islands, the
same on the server (render order) and in the browser (document order). So an
island inside a `<Teleport>`, whose markup lands elsewhere in the document,
is not supported: its position, and so its ids, would differ.

What a person does to the island's form controls before it hydrates is
kept: text typed or filled into a field, a box ticked, a radio or an option
chosen. Just before the mount each such control is set back to what the
server drew, so the hydration matches, and once mounted it gets the
person's value again with an `input` and a `change` event, as the person's
own change would, so `v-model` and a Form's state receive it. A radio
group counts as one value, whichever radio comes first. A control nobody
touched keeps the value its model started with: untouched means as a form
reset would leave it, so a select showing its first option because its
model matches none is untouched.

An island inside another island (a component that uses one, shown in an
island) is not an island of its own: it draws its component in place, and
the outer island hydrates it with the rest of itself.

The page inlines the CSS of everything the island's component uses, not
only what it draws on the server, since the browser may draw the rest later
(a menu that opens, a field that appears). A name taken from the `@weft/ui`
index, `import { Button } from '@weft/ui'`, brings that component's
stylesheet and those of what it draws with, not every component's: the
build follows the names through the index, as a bundler's tree-shaking does
(`@weft/ui` declares its scripts free of side effects in its package.json).
`import * as Weft from '@weft/ui'` takes every name, and so every
stylesheet. Outside islands the page carries only the CSS of the components
it renders.

It has no stylesheet of its own: `<weft-island>` is an unstyled element around the component.

components.name: Kbd
components.purpose: A key on the keyboard, for showing shortcuts.
components.use: In help text, menus and tooltips, one Kbd per key of a shortcut.
components.avoid: For code or a value to copy, use a code element.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; show shortcuts only where a keyboard is likely, which the page decides.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: value
props.description: The key: a character (`K`) or a name with a symbol (`command`, `shift`, `option`, `enter`, `backspace`, `tab`, `arrowup`…). The default slot replaces it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

components.notes:
`value` is a character (`K`) or a key name. Names with a symbol draw the
symbol and say the name to assistive technology, which reads symbols poorly:
`command` (⌘), `shift` (⇧), `option` (⌥), `enter` (↵), `backspace` (⌫),
`tab` (⇥) and the arrows `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`.
Any other value is drawn as given. It draws what it is told and never guesses
the reader's operating system, so the server and browser agree. The default
slot replaces the value.

components.name: Link
components.purpose: A link to another page or site, marking itself when it is the current page.
components.use: For navigation, in running text, in a list of pages or a footer.
components.avoid: For an action that changes something, use Button; for a link that should look like a button, use Button with to.

adapts.input: A standalone link (in a list, a footer, a toolbar) gets a hit area of at least 44 px on touch through a pseudo-element; a link in running text keeps its text size and no larger hit area, which would cover the lines around it. Hover styles apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: to
props.description: The address.

props.name: href
props.description: The address, for those who write links as HTML does; `to` wins.

props.name: external
props.description: Another site: adds rel="noopener". Unset, an address with a scheme and host (`https://…`, `//…`) is external.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to open it, as the native attribute: `_blank` for a new tab.

props.name: rel
props.description: The native rel; `noopener` is added for an external link.

props.name: active
props.description: This link is the current page: sets aria-current="page". Unset, the link compares its address with the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: no address, so not focusable, and announced as a disabled link.

props.name: standalone
props.description: Not in running text (a list of links, a footer, a toolbar): drawn as an inline box whose hit area is at least --weft-hit-min on touch. In a sentence, leave it unset, so the hit area does not cover the lines around it.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Followed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while disabled.

components.notes:
**Standalone or in text.** Set `standalone` on a link that stands on its
own: in navigation, a list, a footer, a toolbar. It becomes an inline box
whose hit area reaches `--weft-hit-min` (44 px on touch). Leave it unset in
running text: a larger hit area there would cover the line above and below
and take taps meant for the links on them (WCAG 2.5.8 exempts targets in a
sentence).

The text is the theme's `--weft-color-primary-text`, which it checks for
4.5:1 on the page.

An external link (an address with a scheme and host, `https://…` or `//…`,
or any with `external`) gets `rel="noopener"`, added to any `rel` you give.
`target` passes through as the native attribute.

The link to the page the browser is on gets `aria-current="page"`. It is
worked out in the browser after mounting, so the server's markup and the
first client render agree; on a page with no JavaScript the server cannot
know, so set `active` where the layout knows the current page. `active`
always wins over the comparison.

**Disabled:** no address and no target, so it leaves the tab order;
announced as a disabled link (`role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`); a click
does nothing.

**Keyboard:** a native anchor, so Tab reaches it and Enter follows it.

**In a Form** that is disabled or busy (submitting), a Link is disabled, so
it cannot navigate mid-submit: a disabled fieldset leaves links alone, so the
Link reads the Form itself.

components.name: Listbox
components.purpose: A list of options always shown, to choose one or several from, with an optional filter field above it.
components.use: For a choice that deserves the room of a visible list (a few to a few thousand options), in a form or a side panel; with `filter` when the list is long.
components.avoid: When the list should open from a field, use Select or Combobox; for two to five options, RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup; for actions, DropdownMenu or CommandPalette.

adapts.input: Options are at least --weft-hit-min tall on pointer and 48 px on touch, with larger text; the pointer highlights the option under it.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container and scrolls past 18rem tall; labels and descriptions are cut with an ellipsis.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or objects with `label`, `value`, `description`, `icon`, `disabled`, `type: 'label' | 'separator'`; or groups of them.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen value, bound with `v-model`; an array with `multiple`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Choose several: `v-model` is an array, and choosing toggles.

props.name: valueKey
props.description: Read an object's value at this key; without it the object itself is the value.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: Read an object's label at this key.

props.name: descriptionKey
props.description: Read an object's description at this key.

props.name: by
props.description: Compare values by this key, or with this function; by default in depth.

props.name: filter
props.description: A search field above the list that filters it.

props.name: searchTerm
props.description: The filter's text, bound with `v-model:search-term`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The filter's placeholder.

props.name: filterFields
props.description: Search these keys of each item; by default its label.

props.name: ignoreFilter
props.description: Show the items as given while searching: the app filters them (async search).

props.name: createItem
props.description: Offer the search as a new item (emits `create`): when nothing matches, or `'always'`; `{ position: 'top' }` puts it first.

props.name: loading
props.description: Items are on their way: `aria-busy`, and a spinner in place of an empty list.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be chosen, and it takes no focus.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set.

props.name: loop
props.description: The arrows wrap round at the ends.

props.name: virtualize
props.description: Draw only the rows in view: by default past 200 options; an object sets `estimateSize` (px, the row height to start from; rows then grow to the tallest measured) and `overscan`.

props.name: selectionBehavior
props.description: With multiple: `toggle`, choosing toggles; `replace`, the choice follows the arrows and a press (Ctrl toggles, Shift extends).

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon marking chosen options, in place of the drawn check.

props.name: id
props.description: The list's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its value submits under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is required (aria-required).

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Chosen: the value, or the array of values with `multiple`.

emits.name: update:searchTerm
emits.description: The filter's text changed.

emits.name: create
emits.description: The create option was chosen, with the search as the new item's label.

emits.name: highlight
emits.description: The active option changed: its item, or undefined when none is active.

components.notes:
`items` are values (`'Apple'`) or objects (`{ label, value, description,
icon, disabled }`), or groups of them (an array of arrays), drawn with
separators between; an object with `type: 'label'` is its group's heading
and `type: 'separator'` a line. Without `value-key` an object is itself the
value; `label-key` and `description-key` read other keys (dotted paths
work), and `by` compares values by a key or a function. Bind the choice with
`v-model` (an array with `multiple`).

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Listbox pattern. The list is one tab stop and
keeps focus; `aria-activedescendant` names the active option, drawn
highlighted. Inside a FormField the list is named by the label
(`aria-labelledby`) and described by the description and error.

**Keyboard.** ArrowDown and ArrowUp move (with `loop` they wrap), Home and
End go to the ends, Page Down and Page Up move ten, typing jumps to the
option whose label starts so; disabled options are skipped. Enter and Space
choose; with `multiple` they toggle. Focusing the list makes the chosen
option active, else the first.

**Several at once.** With `multiple` the APG's recommended keys work too:
Shift+ArrowDown and Shift+ArrowUp move and toggle the option reached,
Shift+Space chooses every option from the last one chosen to the active
one, Ctrl+A (Cmd+A) chooses every option (and again none), and Ctrl+Arrow
moves without choosing, Ctrl+Space toggling; a Shift+press chooses a range
and a Ctrl+press (Cmd+press) toggles one. `selection-behavior="replace"`
makes the choice follow the arrows and a plain press, Shift extending it
from where it started.

**Filter.** With `filter` a search field above the list takes focus instead
(`role="combobox"`, controlling the list); typing filters by label (or
`filter-fields`), ignoring case and accents, the closest matches first, and
the arrows and Enter work from the field. `v-model:search-term` binds the
search; `ignore-filter` leaves the filtering to the app. `create-item` offers
what was typed as a new option, emitting `create`. When nothing is (or
matches) the `empty` slot shows, by default "No results", in a status that
assistive technology announces; `loading` shows a spinner there and sets
`aria-busy`.

**Long lists.** Past 200 options only the rows in view are drawn, over a
spacer as tall as the list. Rows share one height: an estimate from the size
(48 px on touch; `virtualize: { estimateSize }` sets it), grown to the
tallest row drawn so far (a larger font, a taller `item` slot), and at least
--weft-hit-min; when the estimate, the list's width or the page's fonts
change they are measured again from the estimate, so they can get smaller
too. Options carry `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`, counted
within their group, and the active option is always drawn (with its group's
heading), so `aria-activedescendant` never names a missing element.
`virtualize` forces it either way; `{ overscan }` sets how many rows are
drawn past each edge.

With a `name` (or its FormField's) the value submits in hidden inputs, one
per value. The slots `item`, `item-leading`, `item-label`, `item-trailing`
and `create-item-label` replace parts of an option. Select, Combobox and
CommandPalette draw their lists with it.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.purpose: A site's or an app's main links, as a bar whose groups open as lists, or as a sidebar column.
components.use: For the main navigation in a header (horizontal) or a sidebar (vertical).
components.avoid: For actions, use DropdownMenu; for a page's place in the site, Breadcrumb; for a whole app frame, AppShell, which draws one.

adapts.input: On touch every item is at least --weft-hit-min tall, in the bar and in an open list. On a narrow touch screen a horizontal menu is one menu button that opens the items as a column in a Sheet from the start side. A change of input with a list or the sheet open closes it and keeps focus on the same item in the new form.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Horizontal on a narrow touch screen it becomes the menu button and sheet; on a narrow pointer screen it stays a bar, scrolling sideways when it overflows. Before mounting CSS picks the form from the viewport. Vertical, it fills its container.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, or groups of them (an array of arrays), drawn apart: `{ label, to, icon, active, badge, children, … }`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal`: a bar of links and disclosure buttons. `vertical`: a column, as in a sidebar.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Vertical only: icons alone, for a collapsed sidebar; the labels stay for assistive technology and show in tooltips.

props.name: label
props.description: The landmark's name, for assistive technology (and the sheet's title on a narrow touch screen).

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: The name of the menu button on a narrow touch screen.

emits.name: select
emits.description: An item was chosen: a link followed or a button pressed.

components.notes:
`items` are `NavItem`s, or groups of them (an array of arrays) drawn apart:
`{ label, to, target, icon, active, disabled, badge, description, children,
defaultOpen, onSelect }`; `type: 'label'` is a heading over a vertical group.
An item with neither `to` nor `children` is a button that calls `onSelect`.
`label` names the landmark (`Main`); `menu-label` the narrow menu button.
It emits `select(item, event)` when a link is followed or a button pressed
(in the narrow sheet too), and the `item` slot replaces an item's label.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG **Disclosure Navigation** pattern: links stay
links, and an item with children is a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`,
`aria-controls`) that opens a list of links. There is no `menu` role.

**Current page.** Items are Weft Links: `active` sets `aria-current="page"`;
unset, a link compares its address with the browser's, after mounting. An
item whose child is the current page is drawn as current too.

**Forms.** Once mounted the nav says which it draws in `data-form`:

- `bar` (horizontal, on pointer and on wide touch screens): a row of links
  and disclosure buttons; an open list floats under its button (fixed, so a
  scrolling parent does not clip it). One list is open at a time; it closes
  when focus leaves it, on a press outside, when Escape is pressed (focus
  back on its button) and when one of its links is chosen.
- `sheet` (horizontal on a narrow touch screen): the menu button and Sheet.
- `column` (vertical): a list opens below its button, rendered and hidden
  with `hidden="until-found"`, so find-in-page opens it. A group starts open
  with `defaultOpen` or when it holds the current page (by `active`, or by
  the browser's address once mounted), and follows new `items`. `collapsed`
  draws icons alone: labels stay for assistive technology and show in a
  Tooltip on pointer, and a group's list floats beside its button.

Before mounting there is no `data-form`: the server renders the bar and the
menu button, and CSS shows the menu button in place of the bar on a narrow
touch viewport (`max-width: 639.98px` and `pointer: coarse`).

**Keyboard.** Every item is in the tab order. In the bar, Left and Right
also move between the items (mirrored right to left), Home and End to the
ends; ArrowDown on a disclosure button opens its list and focuses its first
link (ArrowUp its last). In a column, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move over the
visible items; in a collapsed column the forward arrow opens a list. In an
open list ArrowDown and ArrowUp move (wrapping), Home and End go to the
ends, and Escape closes it back to its button. Enter and Space press a
button, as native buttons do.

components.name: OverlayPanel
components.purpose: The inside of a modal panel: a header with the heading, actions and close button, a body that scrolls, and a footer.
components.use: Inside a modal surface of your own that should look like Dialog, Sheet and Drawer, which render it themselves.
components.avoid: To open a dialog, use Dialog, Sheet or Drawer; for a card on the page, Card.

adapts.input: Its close button's hit area is at least 44 px on touch.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; the body scrolls when the panel is short.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title.

props.name: titleId
props.description: The id the heading carries, for the overlay's aria-labelledby.

props.name: descriptionId
props.description: The id the description carries, for the overlay's aria-describedby.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

emits.name: close
emits.description: The close button was pressed, or a slot called `close()`.

components.notes:
`title` and `description` are the heading; the `header` slot replaces both.
`title-id` goes on whatever heading renders (the `<h2>`, or the element
around the header slot), and `description-id` on the description, so the
overlay's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` always name something.
`close` shows a CloseButton; it, and `close()` in the `body` and `footer`
slots, emit `close`. The `actions` slot sits before the close button.

components.name: Page
components.purpose: The main landmark of a page, with its title, description, actions and content.
components.use: Once per page, as the outermost layout component, so the page has one main, one h1 and the surface's width and spacing.
components.avoid: For a titled part inside a page, use Section; for a box of related content, use Card.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: On landing the content is centred at up to 1200 px with wider gaps between sections; on app it fills the width with tighter gaps.
adapts.width: Nothing changes in the component itself; the header's actions wrap under the title when they do not fit beside it.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's heading, rendered as its h1 (an h2 inside a WeftProvider marked `inset`).

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title saying what the page is for.

components.notes:
The `title` renders as the page's `h1`. Give the `header` slot to replace the
title and description with your own markup, and the `actions` slot for
buttons beside them.

Inside a WeftProvider marked `inset` (a preview of a page drawn inside
another, such as a gallery's stage) it renders a `<div>` rather than
`<main>`, and its title as an `h2`, so the page around keeps one main and
one h1.

components.name: Pagination
components.purpose: Buttons to move through the pages of a long list.
components.use: Under a table or a list of results that loads a page at a time.
components.avoid: For a feed a reader scrolls, load more as they reach the end; for steps of a task, use Stepper.

adapts.input: Every button is at least --weft-hit-min tall on touch (Button's rule).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: When the viewport is narrow it shows at most one page each side of the current one and drops the first and last buttons; the row wraps when it must.

props.name: page
props.description: The current page, from 1, bound with `v-model:page`.

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: The page shown at first when `v-model:page` is not bound.

props.name: total
props.description: How many items there are in all.

props.name: itemsPerPage
props.description: How many items a page holds.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: How many pages to show on each side of the current one.

props.name: showEdges
props.description: Always show the first and last pages, with ellipses for the gaps.

props.name: showControls
props.description: Show the first, previous, next and last buttons.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every button is disabled.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the other pages and the controls.

props.name: variant
props.description: The variant of the other pages and the controls.

props.name: activeTone
props.description: The colour of the current page.

props.name: activeVariant
props.description: The variant of the current page.

props.name: to
props.description: The address of a page: the buttons become links to it.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says, for assistive technology; give some or all to translate them.

emits.name: update:page
emits.description: Another page was chosen.

components.notes:
Bind the current page with `v-model:page` (from 1). `total` is the number
of items and `items-per-page` the size of a page. `sibling-count` (2) pages
show on each side of the current one; `show-edges` always shows the first
and last, with an ellipsis for each gap, keeping the row the same length.
`show-controls` (on) adds first, previous, next and last. `to(page)` makes
every button a link to that page's address. `variant` and `tone` draw the
other pages, `active-variant` and `active-tone` the current one; `labels`
translate the words for assistive technology.

It is a `nav` landmark (`Pagination`). The current page says
`aria-current="page"`; each page button is named `Page n`; the ellipses are
hidden from assistive technology. The controls at an end are disabled, and
`disabled` disables every button. **Keyboard:** each is a button (or a
link), in the tab order; Enter and Space press it.

`pageRange(page, count, siblings, edges)` is the same arithmetic, exported.

components.name: PinInput
components.purpose: A short code typed one character per box.
components.use: For a one-time code, a verification code or a PIN.
components.avoid: For a password or anything longer than about eight characters, use Input.

adapts.input: Every box is its own target, so md and sm boxes are 44 px square on touch (36 and 28 px on pointer); with type number a number pad comes up.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: The boxes stay in one row.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The code, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The code to start with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: length
props.description: How many boxes.

props.name: type
props.description: `number` takes digits only and brings up a number pad; `text` takes letters and digits.

props.name: mask
props.description: Hide what is typed, as a password field does.

props.name: otp
props.description: A one-time code: lets the browser fill it from a message (autocomplete="one-time-code").

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in each empty box.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: the joined code posts under it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: every box natively disabled.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`, on each box.

props.name: boxLabel
props.description: A box's name for assistive technology; `{n}` is its number and `{count}` how many there are.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A box changed: the joined code.

emits.name: complete
emits.description: Every box is filled: the code.

components.notes:
Bind the joined code with `v-model`; `complete` fires once every box is
filled. `length` sets how many boxes (5). `type="number"` takes digits only;
`mask` hides what is typed; `otp` lets the browser fill a one-time code from
a message (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`).

**Keyboard:** typing a character fills the box and moves to the next;
Backspace clears the box, or steps back and clears the one before when it is
empty; Delete clears the box; Left and Right move (swapped in a right-to-left
document); Home and End go to the first and last box. A paste or an autofill
fills the boxes from the one it lands in, dropping characters the type does
not take.

The boxes form a `role="group"`, named by its FormField's label; each box is
named by its place (`box-label`, "Character 1 of 6"). With `name` the code
posts from a hidden input.

components.name: Popover
components.purpose: Content that floats beside a trigger, opened by a press: filters, a short form, details.
components.use: For a small panel of controls or information tied to one button, which the user opens, uses and closes.
components.avoid: For a list of actions, use DropdownMenu; for a short hint on hover, Tooltip; for a task that needs the user's full attention, Dialog.

adapts.input: On pointer it floats beside the trigger and is not modal. On touch the same content is a bottom sheet over a backdrop, modal, with `title` as its heading. The input can change while it is open; what is inside keeps its state and focus.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Floating, it stays within the room left on its side, flipping and sliding to stay in view; as a sheet it is the viewport's width.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where it floats against the trigger on pointer: `bottom`, `top-start`, … (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: offset
props.description: The gap to the trigger, in px.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the content for assistive technology; on touch it is the sheet's heading too.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press outside close it.

props.name: modal
props.description: Modal on pointer too: focus is trapped and the page does not scroll. On touch it is always modal.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Move focus into the content when it opens (on pointer): to the element marked `data-weft-autofocus`, else the first one; false keeps focus where it is, as a combobox's input needs.

props.name: anchor
props.type: { getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect /** For a point: the element it belongs to, whose scrolling and direction the overlay follows. */ contextElement?: Element }
props.description: Float against this element or point instead of the trigger.

props.name: mode
props.description: `click`: a press on the trigger toggles it. `hover`: the pointer over the trigger or the content opens it too, without moving focus.

props.name: openDelay
props.description: In hover mode, ms of hover before it opens.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: In hover mode, ms after the pointer leaves before it closes.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Draw an arrow pointing at the trigger (floating form only).

props.name: portal
props.description: Draw it in the overlay layer at the end of the body; false draws it in place, and an open one on the server too.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, a press outside or focus leaving.

components.notes:
The default slot is the trigger, one element (a Button); a press on it
toggles the popover, and it carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`,
`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The `content` slot is what it shows,
and gets `close()`. Bind `v-model:open` to open it from code; `anchor`
positions it against another element or a point. A press on an anchor
element is not a press outside, so the component that owns that element
(a Select's button, a Combobox's field) decides what it does.

The content renders into `#weft-overlays` at the end of the body (created
when first needed), only once mounted, so the server renders none of it. It
is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or an `aria-label`); attributes go to
it.

**Focus.** On open, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside, or to
the content itself (`auto-focus="false"` keeps it where it is, as a combobox
does). On pointer it is not modal: Tab can leave, and focus leaving closes it
(unless it went to an overlay opened from inside). With `modal`, or on touch,
focus is trapped and the page does not scroll.

**Closing.** Escape and a press outside close it (`dismissible="false"`
turns both off); a press on its trigger toggles it shut. Focus returns to
the trigger, except after a press outside, which put the user's attention
elsewhere. On touch a press on the backdrop closes it and does return focus.

**Hover mode.** `mode="hover"` opens it too while the pointer is over the
trigger or the content (after `open-delay`, 100 ms) and closes it when the
pointer has left both (after `close-delay`, 200 ms), without moving focus.
A click on the trigger while the hover has it open pins it open (the pointer
leaving no longer closes it; the next click does), and on touch it is pressed
as ever. `arrow` and `offset` can change while it is open. `arrow` draws
an arrow pointing at the trigger. When it starts open (`default-open`) it
does not take focus, so a page that hydrates keeps its own. Modal, the page
behind is inert. It fades out when it closes, unless motion is reduced.

`placement` is a floating-ui placement (`bottom`, `top-start`, …); `start`
and `end` follow the text direction.

`:portal="false"` renders it where it stands instead, and an open one
(`default-open`) on the server too, so a page can show it open with no
script. Until mounted it has no floating coordinates: it hangs from the
element its trigger is in (which becomes its containing block), below it
and from its start edge, from its end edge for an `-end` placement, above
it for a `top` one; once mounted it is positioned as ever. As a touch sheet
over its backdrop it stays `position: fixed`, so an ancestor with
`contain: paint` or a transform keeps it inside (a picture of a phone).
In place it is part of the page: it makes nothing inert and does not lock
the page's scroll (both would reach the popover itself); as a sheet its focus
trap still keeps focus in it.

components.name: Progress
components.purpose: A bar showing how far a task has got, or that it is under way when that is unknown.
components.use: For uploads, imports, multi-step work and quotas, where the reader waits or watches.
components.avoid: For a short wait inside a control, use Spinner; for loading content, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; the bar fills the width it is given.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: How far along, from 0 to `max`; `null` or unset for unknown (indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: The value at completion.

props.name: label
props.description: What it measures, for assistive technology ("Uploading report.pdf").

props.name: tone
props.description: The bar's colour and what it says.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the bar's thickness.

props.name: status
props.description: Show the percentage beside the bar (determinate only).

components.notes:
Bind the value with `v-model` (or `model-value`), from 0 to `max` (100);
values outside are clamped. `null` or no value is indeterminate: a bar that
sweeps, which stands still at full length, dimmed, under reduced motion.
`status` shows the percentage beside the bar.

It is a `progressbar` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and, when
determinate, `aria-valuenow`. Name it with `label` ("Uploading report.pdf")
or an `aria-labelledby`. The bar fills along the inline direction, so from
the right in a right-to-left document.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.purpose: One choice among a few options, all in view.
components.use: For a choice of two to five options the reader should compare at a glance (a plan, a shipping speed).
components.avoid: For many options, use a select; for on or off, use Switch or Checkbox.

adapts.input: Each row is at least 44 px tall on touch, and each radio's hit area 44 px square.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Horizontal groups wrap onto more rows when narrow.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen value, bound with `v-model`; undefined or null when none is.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value chosen at first when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or `{ value, label, description, disabled }`.

props.name: legend
props.description: The group's name, shown above it; inside a FormField the field's label names it instead.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name the radios share; a FormField's applies, else one is generated.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the chosen radio.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` (a column) or `horizontal` (a wrapping row). The arrow keys work the same either way.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every radio.

props.name: required
props.description: A choice must be made: the native `required` on the radios.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A radio was chosen, by press, Space or an arrow key.

components.notes:
Bind the chosen value with `v-model`; give the options as `items` - values,
or `{ value, label, description, disabled }`.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA radio group pattern): the group is one tab stop,
on the chosen radio or else the first. Down and Right move to the next radio
and choose it, Up and Left to the previous, wrapping at the ends and
skipping disabled radios; in a right-to-left document Left and Right swap.
Focus arriving by Tab or a click chooses nothing by itself; Space chooses
the focused radio.

The radios are native, sharing `name` (one is generated when not given), so
they post with a plain form. The group is `role="radiogroup"`, named by
`legend` or by its FormField's label, described by the field's description, hint and
error, and `aria-required` when the field (or `required`) asks.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.purpose: A box whose content scrolls inside it, with the browser's own scrolling and thin themed scrollbars.
components.use: For a long list in a fixed-height panel, a wide strip of cards that scrolls sideways, a code block or a log.
components.avoid: For the page itself, let the page scroll; for thousands of rows, use Table or Listbox, which render only those in view.

adapts.input: On touch the browser's own overlay scrollbars and momentum scrolling apply; nothing is drawn over them.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; it scrolls whatever overflows its box.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way it scrolls: `vertical` (default), `horizontal` or `both`.

props.name: label
props.description: Its name, for assistive technology: it becomes a region. Give one when it is a tab stop.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The most it may be tall before it scrolls, any CSS length; or set its height from outside.

props.name: shadow
props.description: Fade the edges that have more content beyond them (block edges, inline edges, or all four for `both`).

components.notes:
It is the browser's scrolling, not a drawn one: wheel, touch, momentum,
scroll anchoring, find-in-page and the keyboard all work as they do on the
page. The scrollbars are thin and drawn in the theme's border colour
(`scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color`, with the WebKit pseudo-elements
where those are missing).

`orientation` is `vertical` (default), `horizontal` or `both`. Give it a
height from outside, or `max-height`: its viewport fills it. While its content overflows it is a
tab stop (`tabindex="0"`), so a keyboard alone can scroll it with the
arrows, Page Up and Down, Home, End and Space; once it fits it leaves the
tab order. With `label` it is a named region, which assistive technology
lists; give one whenever it is a tab stop.

`shadow` fades each edge with more content beyond it: the block edges when
vertical, the inline edges when horizontal (mirrored right to left), all
four with `both`. A fade is an overlay over the content, not a mask, so the
scrollbars (whose thickness it measures) and the focus ring stay clear; it
runs from `--weft-scroll-fade-color` (the page background by default; set
it to a card's surface when the area sits on one) to transparent. Rows that
must render only while in view belong in Table or Listbox, which window long
lists themselves.

components.name: Select
components.purpose: A button showing the chosen value that opens a list to choose one, or several, from.
components.use: For a choice from a known list in a form (a country, a status, a size), where the list is too long for radio buttons and nobody needs to type to find an option.
components.avoid: When people search the list or type their own value, use Combobox; for two to five options always in view, RadioGroup; for actions, DropdownMenu.

adapts.input: On pointer the list floats under the button, at least as wide, focus staying on the button. On touch it is a modal bottom sheet (focus trapped, the page behind inert) with the field's label as its title and a search field at the top, which takes focus and filters; options are 48 px tall. The input can change while it is open; the active option and the choice stay, and focus moves to the button or the search field.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: The button fills its container's width; the floating list stays within the room left, flipping above when there is none below; the sheet is the viewport's width.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or objects with `label`, `value`, `description`, `icon`, `disabled`, `type: 'label' | 'separator'`; or groups of them.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen value, bound with `v-model`; an array with `multiple`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Choose several: `v-model` is an array, choosing toggles, and the list stays open.

props.name: valueKey
props.description: Read an object's value at this key; an empty string makes the object itself the value.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: Read an object's label at this key.

props.name: descriptionKey
props.description: Read an object's description at this key.

props.name: by
props.description: Compare values by this key, or with this function; by default in depth.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while nothing is chosen.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: The search field's placeholder, in the touch sheet.

props.name: searchInput
props.description: A search field at the top of the touch sheet; false leaves it out, and the list itself takes focus.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the value. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon in place of the chevron.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon marking chosen options, in place of the drawn check.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: a spinner in place of the chevron, and aria-busy.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Cannot be opened or changed.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is required (aria-required).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its value submits under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The button's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points here.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the list floats on pointer (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: loop
props.description: The arrows wrap round at the ends.

props.name: virtualize
props.description: Draw only the rows in view: by default past 200 options; an object sets `estimateSize` (px, the row height to start from) and `overscan`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Chosen: the value, or the array of values with `multiple`.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The value changed by a choice.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: Focus left the button and its list.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The button took focus.

components.notes:
`items` are values or objects (`{ label, value, description, icon,
disabled }`), or groups of them, with `type: 'label'` headings and
`type: 'separator'` lines, as in Listbox. An object's value is read at
`value` (`value-key` names another key; `value-key=""` makes the object
itself the value). Bind the choice with `v-model` (an array with `multiple`,
which shows the chosen labels joined by commas and keeps the list open),
and the list with `v-model:open`.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Select-Only Combobox pattern: a `button` with
`role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` and, while
open, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`. Inside a FormField the
label is `for` the button and names the list; the description and error
describe the button, and an error marks it `aria-invalid`.

**Keyboard.** Closed: ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Enter and Space open the list on the
chosen option (else the first), Home and End on the first and the last, and
typing opens it on the option whose label starts so. Open: the arrows,
Home, End, Page Up and Page Down move, skipping disabled options; typing
jumps; Enter and Space choose and close (with `multiple` they toggle);
Alt+ArrowUp chooses and closes; Tab chooses and moves on; Escape closes
without choosing. Focus stays on the button throughout (on touch, on the
sheet's search field, and back on the button when it closes).

A press on the button toggles the list; a press outside closes it, and so
does focus leaving. `disabled` blocks the press and every key (the button is
natively disabled); `loading` draws a spinner in place of the chevron and
sets `aria-busy`. `search-input="false"` leaves the touch sheet's search
field out; the list then takes focus itself. Choosing the value already
chosen emits no `change`. With a `name` (or its FormField's) the value submits in
hidden inputs. Past 200 options only the rows in view are drawn, the active
one always. The `default` slot draws the value on the button, `leading`
and `trailing` its ends, and `item`, `item-leading`, `item-label`,
`item-trailing` and `empty` the list's parts.

components.name: Separator
components.purpose: A rule that separates content, with an optional label or icon in its middle.
components.use: Between groups of content that need a named break, such as "or" between two sign-in methods, or a date in a feed.
components.avoid: For a plain rule, use Divider; for space alone, use the gap of a Stack or Grid; for a new titled part, use Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the label follows the surface's type scale.

props.name: label

props.name: orientation

props.name: decorative

components.notes:

`separator` with `aria-orientation`, named by `label`; `decorative` hides it
from assistive technology (`role="none"`, `aria-hidden="true"`), for a rule
that separates nothing a reader needs told about. `orientation="vertical"` stretches to the height
of its row.
