components.name: Sheet
components.purpose: A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the viewport: a slideover from the side, or a bottom sheet.
components.use: For navigation on small screens, filters, a detail view or a form that should keep the page visible beside it.
components.avoid: For a short decision, use Dialog or ConfirmDialog; for content tied to one button on a large screen, Popover.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; on touch its close button's hit area is at least 44 px. Popover and DropdownMenu render as a bottom sheet on touch with this stylesheet.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A side sheet is at most 24rem wide, the full width when the viewport is narrower; a top or bottom sheet is the viewport's width and at most 85% of its height.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, which names the sheet. Without one or a header slot, give the sheet an `aria-label`.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, which describes the sheet.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button (×) in the header.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press on the backdrop close it.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Dim the page with a backdrop; without one it is still modal.

props.name: side
props.description: The side it comes from: `start` and `end` (the inline sides, mirrored right to left), `top` or `bottom`.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, the backdrop or a close.

components.notes:
`side` is `start` or `end` (the inline sides, so mirrored in a right-to-left
document), `top` or `bottom`; the default is `end`. Otherwise it is used as
Dialog is: the default slot is the trigger, or bind `v-model:open`; `title`
and `description` name and describe it; `header`, `actions`, `body` and
`footer` slots, the last two with `close()`.

It is a modal dialog (WAI-ARIA APG, Dialog (Modal)): focus is trapped inside,
the page does not scroll, and Escape, the backdrop and the close button
close it (`dismissible="false"` keeps Escape and the backdrop from it), with
focus back on the trigger. The page behind is inert while it is open, and
it slides back out when it closes, unless motion is reduced; `overlay="false"`
draws no backdrop. The body scrolls when long.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading.
components.use: Where text, an avatar or a card will appear, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.
components.avoid: For a wait with no shape to show, use Spinner; when the progress is known, use Progress.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; its default height is one line of the surface's text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; without a width it fills its container.

props.name: width

props.name: circle

components.notes:

and one line (1em) high. `circle` makes it round, for an avatar.

It pulses, and stands still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. It is hidden

loading, and remove it when the content arrives.

components.name: Slider
components.purpose: A value, or a range between two values, picked along a track.
components.use: For a value where the position matters more than the exact number (volume, a price range).
components.avoid: For an exact number, use InputNumber; for a few named steps, use RadioGroup.

adapts.input: The thumb is drawn 16 px (12 sm, 20 lg) on pointer and 24 px on touch (--weft-thumb-min), where a finger covers it; on touch its hit area and the track's grow to 44 px through pseudo-elements, and the slider is 44 px tall.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; vertical sliders are 160 px tall.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The value, or an array of values for a range, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value to start with when `v-model` is not bound; an array for a range.

props.name: min
props.description: The start of the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The end of the track.

props.name: step
props.description: The values it moves between, counted from `min`.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: For a range: the fewest steps kept between neighbouring thumbs.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (min at the inline start) or `vertical` (min at the bottom).

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Each thumb's name for assistive technology; for a range the default is "Minimum", "Value 2 of 3"… and "Maximum". A single thumb takes the Slider's own aria-label, or its FormField's label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: each value posts under it from a hidden input.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the track's thickness and the thumb's size.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the filled part and the thumbs.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: out of the tab order, and presses do nothing.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A thumb moved, by key, press or drag.

emits.name: change
emits.description: A move ended: a key press, or a drag let go; the final value.

components.notes:
Bind a number with `v-model`, or an array for a range: a thumb is drawn per
value, thumbs never pass each other (`min-steps-between-thumbs` keeps a gap),
and the track between them fills.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA slider pattern): each thumb is a `role="slider"`
in the tab order. Right and Up raise it by `step`, Left and Down lower it,
Page Up and Page Down move ten steps, Home and End go to the ends. In a
right-to-left document Left and Right swap, and the track fills from the
right. Each thumb's `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are its neighbours.

**Pointer:** a press on the track moves the nearest thumb there, on a step,
and drags it until let go. `update:modelValue` fires as it moves; `change`
fires once a move ends (a key press, or a drag let go).

Thumbs are named by `thumb-labels`, or for a range "Minimum" and "Maximum"
(a thumb between them "Value 2 of 3");
a single thumb takes the Slider's own `aria-label`, or its FormField's label.
In a FormField a range's thumbs are named by the label and their own name
("Price Minimum"). With `name`
each value posts from a hidden input.

components.purpose: A turning ring for work in progress of unknown length.
components.use: Inside something that is loading, or alone where content will appear; Button shows one itself when loading.
components.avoid: When the progress is known, use Progress; for the shape of content still loading, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the spinner is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label

components.notes:

(`aria-hidden`); with one it is a `status` that announces the label
politely. `size` is `sm` (16 px), `md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it
the spinner is 1.25em. Under reduced motion it turns slowly rather than
freezing, since a still ring reads as stuck.

components.name: Stack
components.purpose: Lays its children out in a column or a row with a gap from the spacing scale.
components.use: For any run of things one after another, a form's fields, a toolbar's buttons, a card's lines, instead of margins or a wrapper with its own CSS.
components.avoid: For columns that should reflow with the space available, use Grid; for a page or a titled part of one, use Page or Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; hit targets are the children's own.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the gap scale is the same spacing tokens on landing and app.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a row stays a row, so give it wrap when its children may not fit a narrow container.

props.name: direction
props.description: Lay the children out top to bottom (`column`) or along the line (`row`).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, from the spacing scale (`--weft-space-*`).

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment of the children.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis distribution of the children; `between` pushes them to the ends.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let a row wrap onto more lines when its children do not fit.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render, for semantics: `ul`, `nav`, `form`.

components.notes:
`gap` takes the spacing scale (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8, from `--weft-space-*`).
`align` and `justify` work along the cross and main axes as in flexbox, and
`as` renders another element, such as `ul` or `nav`, for the right semantics.

components.name: StatCard
components.purpose: One figure that matters on a card, with how it changed and an optional sparkline.
components.use: In a row of key figures at the top of a dashboard (revenue, active customers, open tickets); it replaces the hand-built stat cards of admin panels such as Negenet's.
components.avoid: For many figures to compare, use Table; for a figure inside a sentence, write the sentence.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; it is not interactive (a link in its footer follows Link's rules).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; the figure and label follow the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its grid cell, and a long figure wraps rather than overflow; lay several out with Grid, which stacks them when narrow.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure is: "Revenue".

props.name: value
props.description: The figure: a number (formatted for the locale) or text as it should read ("$1.2M").

props.name: delta
props.description: How much it changed, as a number: 4 for a 4% rise, -2 for a fall.

props.name: deltaUnit
props.description: After the delta's number: `%` (default), ` pts`, or nothing.

props.name: invert
props.description: Less is better (churn, errors): a fall is good news, drawn in the success tone.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence after the delta: "vs last month".

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label.

props.name: loading
props.description: Still counting: a skeleton in place of the value, and aria-busy.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says; give some or all to translate them.

components.notes:
`label` names the figure and `value` is the figure: a number is formatted
for the locale (a WeftProvider's, else `en-US`, so the server and the
browser agree), text shows as given (`$1.2M`). It is a description list,
so assistive technology reads the label with the value.

`delta` is how it changed, as a number (4 for a 4% rise, -2 for a fall),
followed by `delta-unit` (`%`). Its sign picks the tone: success up, danger
down, neutral for 0; `invert` swaps them for figures where less is better
(churn, errors). It is drawn as `+4%` with an arrow and said as "up 4%",
"down 2%" or "no change" (translate with `labels`). `description` follows
the delta ("vs last month"). `icon` (or the leading slot) sits before the
label.

The `sparkline` slot holds a small chart under the figure, as wide as the
card, in the primary colour (an svg drawn with `currentColor` follows it);
it is drawing only, hidden from assistive technology, so the figure and the
delta must carry the meaning. `footer` holds a link to the details.
`loading` makes it `aria-busy`, a skeleton in place of the value and no
delta.

components.name: Stepper
components.purpose: The steps of a task done in order, with the current step's content.
components.use: For a checkout, an onboarding, a setup wizard: three to six steps.
components.avoid: For views a reader moves between freely, use Tabs; for where a page sits in a site, Breadcrumb.

adapts.input: Each step button is at least --weft-hit-min tall on touch.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A horizontal stepper stacks vertically when its own width is narrow (under 640 px).

props.name: items
props.description: The steps: `{ title, description, value, icon, content, disabled, slot }`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The current step's value, bound with `v-model`: its `value`, else its index.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The step at first when `v-model` is not bound; default the first.

props.name: linear
props.description: Steps go in order: a press reaches only the steps done and the next one.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (a row, stacked when narrow) or `vertical` (a column).

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the current and completed steps.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: No step can be chosen.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The current step changed.

emits.name: next
emits.description: `next()` moved on, to this step.

emits.name: prev
emits.description: `prev()` moved back, to this step.

components.notes:
`items` are `{ title, description, value, icon, content, disabled, slot }`;
a step's value is its `value`, else its index. Bind the current step with
`v-model`. The `indicator`, `title` and `description` slots replace those
parts of a step, the `content` slot the current step's content, and a slot
named by an item's `slot` renders that step's content.

The steps are an ordered list of buttons; the current one says
`aria-current="step"`, those before it are drawn done (a check), those after
it waiting. `linear` (the default) lets a press reach only the steps done and
the next one; disabled steps are never reached. The component exposes
`next()`, `prev()`, `hasNext` and `hasPrev` (through a template ref), for a
form's Back and Continue buttons, and emits `next` and `prev`.

**Keyboard.** The step buttons are one tab stop: the arrow keys move
between them (Left and Right mirrored right to left), Home and End go to the
ends, Enter and Space choose.

components.name: Switch
components.purpose: On or off, taking effect at once.
components.use: For a setting that applies as soon as it changes (Wi-Fi, notifications).
components.avoid: For a choice sent with a form (accept the terms), use Checkbox.

adapts.input: The track keeps its drawn size; its hit area is at least 44 px square on touch, and the row at least 44 px tall.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a long label wraps beside the track.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: On or off, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The state to start in when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the switch. The default slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the label, which also describes the switch.

props.name: value
props.description: What a form post sends while it is on (default `on`).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour while on.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (the change is being saved): a spinner in the thumb, aria-busy, and no toggling.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`: it must be on.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Turned on or off.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change.

components.notes:
Bind with `v-model`. It is a native checkbox with `role="switch"`, so Space
and its label toggle it, assistive technology reads it as on or off, and it
posts `value` under `name` while on.

**Loading** (the change is being saved) turns a spinner in the thumb, sets
`aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, and blocks a press, Space and the label
alike, while it stays focusable. **Disabled** is native.

The thumb slides to the inline end when on, so to the left in a right-to-left
document.

components.name: Table
components.purpose: Rows of data under column headers, sorted, chosen, paged and loaded from an array or from a server.
components.use: For records a person compares, sorts or acts on in bulk (customers, invoices, devices), from a plain array or a server speaking the wire format.
components.avoid: For a few label–value pairs about one thing, use a description list or StatCard; for items a person reads one by one, use a list of Cards; for a hierarchy, use Tree.

adapts.input: On touch every row is at least --weft-hit-min (44 px) tall, and its checkbox takes a 44 px press (Checkbox's rule).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; `size` sets the row height and text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: When its own box is narrow (under 640 px, even in a side panel on a wide screen) each row becomes a card, a list item of label–value pairs from the same columns, with a Select all checkbox and the sort buttons above the cards; wide again, it is a table again.

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns: `{ key, label, sortable, align, width, accessor, format, rowHeader }`.

props.name: rows
props.description: The rows, sorted and paged on the client.

props.name: fetch
props.description: Asks for a page of rows instead, in the wire format's names (`{ page, per_page, sort, q, filter }` → `{ items, total, page, per_page }`; the last two are optional), so a generated list function fits as it is: paging, sorting, search and filters happen on the server.

props.name: search
props.description: The search text, sent to `fetch` as `q`; empty sends none. Does nothing without `fetch`. A new one goes to page 1.

props.name: filters
props.description: Filters by field name, sent to `fetch` as `filter`; an empty value is no filter. Does nothing without `fetch`. New ones go to page 1.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: A row's key, for selection and rendering: a property name or a function; default the row's `id`, else its place.

props.name: sort
props.description: The sort, in the wire format (`name`, `-since`; null for none), bound with `v-model:sort`.

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: The sort when `v-model:sort` is not bound.

props.name: selectable
props.description: A checkbox on each row, and one in the header for every row shown.

props.name: selected
props.description: The keys of the chosen rows, bound with `v-model:selected`.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: The rows chosen when `v-model:selected` is not bound.

props.name: perPage
props.description: Rows per page: the table pages with a Pagination. With `fetch`, default 20.

props.name: page
props.description: The page, from 1, bound with `v-model:page`.

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: The page shown first when `v-model:page` is not bound.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: skeleton rows until there are rows, and aria-busy.

props.name: empty
props.description: The text shown when there are no rows; the `empty` slot replaces it.

props.name: caption
props.description: The table's caption, which names it (and the list of cards).

props.name: hideCaption
props.description: Draw the caption for assistive technology only.

props.name: sticky
props.description: The header stays in view while the rows scroll inside the table.

props.name: height
props.description: The most the table may be tall before its rows scroll, any CSS length; default 30rem once windowed past 200 rows.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: px of every row once windowed past 200 rows; default from the size (44 at least on touch).

props.name: keyboard
props.description: APG grid: one tab stop, arrow keys between cells. Off: a plain table, every control its own tab stop.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the rows' height.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says; give some or all to translate them.

emits.name: update:sort
emits.description: The sort changed: a header was pressed.

emits.name: update:selected
emits.description: The chosen rows changed.

emits.name: update:page
emits.description: Another page was chosen, or the sort went back to page 1.

emits.name: error
emits.description: `fetch` failed.

components.notes:
`columns` is a typed array: `{ key, label, sortable, align, width,
accessor, format, rowHeader }`. A cell shows `accessor(row)` (default
`row[key]`) as text, or `format(value, row)`; the `<key>-cell` slot draws it
instead (`{ row, value, index, column }`), and `<key>-header` the header. A
`rowHeader` column's cells are `th scope="row"`, and its value names each
row's checkbox ("Select Ada").

**Rows.** Give `rows` (an array), sorted and paged on the client (text in
the WeftProvider's `locale`, en-US without one, numbers and dates by
amount), or `fetch(query)`, which receives the wire format's list query
in its names, `{ page, per_page, sort, q, filter }` (each but `page` and
`per_page` is absent when there is none; `sort` is `name` or `-since`),
and answers the wire format's whole list, `{ items, total, page, per_page }`
(`page` and `per_page` are optional), so paging, sorting, searching and
filtering happen on the server. A list function from the generated client
fits as it is: `:fetch="api.products.list"`. Give the search text as
`search` (sent as `q`) and the filters as `filters` (`{ plan: 'pro' }`,
sent as `filter`); a change asks again. Clearing a filter is setting it to
an empty string or leaving it out: a filter with no value is not sent, and
`{ status: '' }` is the same query as `{}`. With `rows` and no `fetch`,
`search` and `filters` do nothing.
`tableSearch(query)` writes the query as the wire format's search
parameters: `page=2&per_page=20&sort=-since&q=ada&filter[plan]=pro`. It asks
once mounted (the server draws skeleton rows), again whenever the page, the
sort, the search or the filters change, ignores an answer a newer query
overtook, and shows a message with a Try again button (and emits `error`)
when the promise rejects; `refresh()` asks again. `rowKey` (a property name
or a function; default the row's `id`, else its place) keys the rows. The
data source is `useTableData`, exported for a view of its own.

**Sorting.** A sortable header holds a button: ascending, descending, then
as given. The sort is `v-model:sort` in the wire format. On the client it is
stable (equal rows keep their order both ways), numbers and dates by amount,
text numeric-aware and case-blind, empty values last. A press on a header
goes back to page 1, as does a new `search` or new `filters` (with `fetch`); a
parent that sets the page and the sort, the search or the filters together
keeps its page. The sorted header says `aria-sort`; the others say nothing (APG
sortable table).

**Selection.** `selectable` adds a checkbox per row and one in the header,
bound with `v-model:selected` (the rows' keys). The header box is ticked
when every row shown is chosen, indeterminate when some are; it chooses or
clears the rows shown (on this page). Shift+click on a row's box sets every
row from the last one clicked to it, in the order shown. Keys persist
across pages and sorts: a row chosen on page 1 stays chosen on page 3 and
after a new sort. So rows from `fetch` that can be chosen need keys of their
own, an `id` or `rowKey`; without one a row's key is its place on its page,
and development builds warn once.

**Paging.** `per-page` pages the rows with a Pagination under the table
(`v-model:page`), shown when there is more than one page; with `fetch` it
defaults to 20.

**States.** `loading` makes it `aria-busy` and draws skeleton rows (hidden
from assistive technology, a status saying Loading) until there are rows;
rows it already has stay, dimmed. With no rows the `empty` slot (or
`empty`, default "Nothing to show.") fills the body.

**Sticky header.** With `sticky` (on by default) the header stays in view.
With a `height` (or once windowed) the rows scroll inside the table's box
and the header sticks at its top. Without one the box clips rather than
scrolls once mounted, so the header sticks against the page as it scrolls,
below `--weft-table-sticky-top` (set it to a sticky page header's height);
but a table wider than its box must scroll sideways, and then its header
sticks only inside it: give it a `height`. Before it mounts (and on a page
with no island) the box scrolls, so a wide table is never cut off.

**Windowing.** Past 200 rows on a page it renders only the rows in view,
spacer rows standing for the rest (`useVirtualList`): every row is then
`row-height` px (default by size, at least 44 on touch), its text on one
line, the box 30rem tall unless `height` says otherwise, and the table
states `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`. The narrow cards are
not windowed; page long lists.

**Keyboard.** By default it is a plain `<table>` (caption, `th scope`), and
each control in it (sort buttons, checkboxes, controls in cells) is its own
tab stop. With `keyboard` it is an APG grid, one tab stop, so Tab enters and
leaves it in one step: arrows move between cells (mirrored right to left)
and stop at the edges, Home and End go along the row, Ctrl+Home to the first
header cell and Ctrl+End to the last cell of the last row, windowed or not.
The focused cell scrolls into view, and a windowed table keeps its row drawn
when the pointer scrolls it away, so focus is never lost. A sort button or a
checkbox stands in for its cell. Controls a cell slot draws leave the tab
order (`tabindex="-1"`); Enter or F2 on the cell gives them back and focuses
the first, keys pressed in it are its own, and Escape, or focus leaving the
cell, takes them out again. `caption` names the table (and the
list of cards); `hide-caption` keeps it for assistive technology only.
`labels` translate its words.

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: Views of one thing, one shown at a time, picked from a row of tabs.
components.use: For settings pages, a record's details and its history, code in several languages.
components.avoid: To move between pages, use NavigationMenu or links; for sections a reader may open together, use Accordion.

adapts.input: Tabs are at least --weft-hit-min tall on touch; a row too long for its width scrolls sideways.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A vertical tab list goes above the panels when the tabs' own width is narrow (under 640 px), and turns horizontal.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs: `{ label, value, icon, badge, content, disabled, slot }`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The selected tab's value, bound with `v-model`: its `value`, else its index.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab selected at first when `v-model` is not bound; default the first enabled one.

props.name: activation
props.description: `automatic`: focusing a tab selects it. `manual`: Enter, Space or a press selects the focused tab.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (a row above the panels) or `vertical` (a column beside them, above them when narrow).

props.name: variant
props.description: `pill`: tabs in a tinted track, the selected one raised. `link`: an underline marks the selected tab.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the selected tab.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: content
props.description: Draw the panels; false draws the tab list alone (to switch something else).

props.name: keepAlive
props.description: Keep a panel's content mounted, hidden, once it has been shown, so its state survives; by default only the selected panel's content is rendered.

props.name: hash
props.description: Read the selected tab from the address's #fragment, and write it there on a change (replacing the history entry, not adding one). One Tabs per page may: a second warns and leaves the hash alone.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A tab was selected.

components.notes:
`items` are `{ label, value, icon, badge, content, disabled, slot }`; a tab's
value is its `value`, else its index. Bind the selected tab with `v-model`.
The `leading`, default and `trailing` slots replace a tab's icon, label and
badge; the `content` slot a panel's content, and a slot named by an item's
`slot` renders that item's panel. `content: false` draws the tab list alone.
`variant` is `pill` (a tinted track, the default) or `link` (an underline);
`tone` colours the selected tab.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Tabs pattern: a `tablist` (named by the
`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` given to Tabs) with `aria-orientation`,
`tab`s with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and `tabpanel`s named by
their tab, each focusable (`tabindex="0"`).

**Keyboard.** The tab list is one tab stop, on the selected tab. Left and
Right (mirrored right to left), or Up and Down when vertical, move along it,
wrapping and skipping disabled tabs; Home and End go to the ends. With
`activation="automatic"` (the default) the tab focus lands on is selected;
with `manual`, Enter or Space selects it.

**Panels.** Only the selected panel's content is rendered (lazy). With
`keep-alive`, a panel's content stays mounted, hidden, once shown, so a
form's input or a scroll position survives switching away.

**Address.** With `hash`, the address's `#fragment` selects the tab whose
value it names, at mounting and on every `hashchange`, and the selected tab
is written there (replacing the history entry, not adding one). A fragment
naming a disabled tab, or none, is ignored. Off by default. One Tabs per
page owns the hash, the first mounted with `hash`; a second warns once and
leaves the address alone, so give `hash` to one Tabs per page.

components.name: Textarea
components.purpose: Text over several lines, which can grow with what is typed.
components.use: For a message, a description, a note; with autoresize where the length varies.
components.avoid: For one line, use Input; for formatted text, use an editor.

adapts.input: It is never shorter than an md control, so at least 44 px on touch whatever its rows and size.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The text, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: rows
props.description: Lines shown, and with autoresize the fewest it shrinks to.

props.name: autoresize
props.description: Grow with the text, from `rows` up to `maxrows`.

props.name: maxrows
props.description: With autoresize, the most lines it grows to before it scrolls; 0 for no limit.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the text size and padding.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: disabled

props.name: readonly

Bind the text with `v-model` (`.trim` and `.lazy` work). `rows` sets how many
lines show (3). With `autoresize` it grows as text is added, from `rows` up to
`maxrows` (0, the default, for no limit) and then scrolls, and it shrinks
back when text is removed; it cannot be resized by hand then. A template ref
has `focus()`, `resize()` (to fit after being shown) and `textarea`.

In a FormField it takes the field's id, name, description, error and required
state, as Input does. Attributes go to the `<textarea>`.

components.name: Timeline
components.purpose: Events in order, each a dot on a line with its date, title and description, the ones up to now marked done.
components.use: For an order's progress, an account's history or a changelog: what happened, and when.
components.avoid: For steps a person moves through and can go back to, use Stepper; for a log to search and sort, use Table.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; it is not interactive.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A horizontal timeline turns vertical when its own box is narrow, so the text keeps its width.

props.name: items
props.description: The events: `{ date, title, description, icon, value }`, oldest first.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The current item's value (or its place, from 0): those before it are done.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The current item when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` (default) or `horizontal`; vertical whenever its box is narrow.

props.name: reverse
props.description: List the newest first.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the done and current items.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the dots and the text.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says; give some or all to translate them.

components.notes:
`items` are `{ date, title, description, icon, value }`, oldest first;
`reverse` lists the newest first. `date` is text as it should read ("Mar
4", "2 hours ago"). An item with an `icon` draws it in a disc; the others
are dots.

Give the current item with `v-model` (its `value`, or its place from 0):
the items before it are done, drawn in `tone` with their line, and said as
"Done:" before the title (translate with `labels`); the current one is
ringed and says `aria-current="step"`; the later ones are muted. With no
current item every item is drawn alike. The timeline only shows this; it
never changes it.

It is an ordered list; the dots and lines are hidden from assistive
technology. The `indicator`, `date`, `title` and `description` slots draw
an item's parts (`{ item, index }`). `orientation` is `vertical` (default)
or `horizontal`; `size` sets the dots and text.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: One short message that appears for a moment, with an optional action: saved, sent, undone.
components.use: Rendered by Toaster from useToast(); render one yourself only inside a live region of your own.
components.avoid: To show a toast, call useToast().add and put a Toaster in the layout; for a message that must stay, use an inline alert.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; its close button's hit area is at least 44 px on touch.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its Toaster's column.

props.name: title
props.description: The message, in bold.

props.name: description
props.description: More about it, under the title.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `success`, `danger`, …

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text.

props.name: duration
props.description: ms before it leaves on its own; default `--weft-duration-toast`; 0 stays until closed. Changing it starts the time again.

props.name: paused
props.description: Its time stands still: hovered, or focus inside.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons after the text; each closes the toast after it runs.

props.name: progress
props.description: Show the time left as a bar.

props.name: revision
props.description: Counts the message's replacements (useToast sets it); each one starts its time again.

props.name: swipe
props.description: The edge a swipe on touch throws it towards: its Toaster's side.

emits.name: close
emits.description: It has gone: its time ran out, or it was closed, acted on or swiped away.

components.notes:
`title`, `description`, `icon` (a Lucide name), `tone` (a bar at the inline
start), `actions` (buttons, each closing the toast after it runs) and a
close button (× drawn inline; `close="false"` hides it). The default,
`leading` and `actions` slots replace the text, icon and actions.

It emits `close` when it should go: after `duration` ms (by default the
theme's `--weft-duration-toast`, 4000 ms in the neutral theme; 0 stays until
closed), when closed, acted on, swiped away, or on Escape while focus is in
it, once its leave transition has played. Its time stands still while
`paused`, resumes with what it had left, and starts again when its message
is replaced (`revision`, which useToast counts) or `duration` changes. A bar along its bottom edge shows the time left (`progress="false"`
hides it; it is hidden under reduced motion). On touch, a swipe towards
`swipe` (its Toaster's side) past a third of its width, or a flick, throws it
away; short of that it springs back.

components.name: Toaster
components.purpose: Shows the toasts queued with useToast(), in a corner of the viewport, announced to assistive technology.
components.use: Once, in the app's layout; then call useToast().add from anywhere in the browser.
components.avoid: For a message tied to a form or a section, show it there instead.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; toasts' buttons follow Button's touch sizes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: At most 24rem wide, the viewport less a margin when narrower.

props.name: position
props.description: Where toasts stack: a corner, or the middle of the top or bottom edge.

props.name: max
props.description: How many stay at once; a new toast beyond that drops the oldest.

props.name: label
props.description: The region's name for assistive technology.

components.notes:
const toast = useToast()
    toast.add({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your draft is safe.', tone: 'success' })
    toast.add({ title: 'Deleted', actions: [{ label: 'Undo', onClick: restore }] })

`add` returns the toast with its `id`, for `update(id, patch)` and
`remove(id)`; `clear()` empties the queue and `toasts` reads it. Adding a
toast again with the same id (`add({ id: 'saved', … })` on every save), or
updating it, replaces it: its time starts again and it is announced again. A toast
leaves after its `duration`, by default the theme's `--weft-duration-toast`.

The Toaster is a region named "Notifications" (`label`). A new toast is
announced without moving focus, by type, as in Nuxt UI: `background`
politely, `foreground` at once (assertively); a `danger` toast is
foreground unless it says otherwise. While the pointer is over it or focus
is inside it, no toast's time runs. F8 moves focus to it, to reach a toast's
actions, even while a modal is open (the region is exempt from its focus
trap and is never made inert); when the focused toast goes, focus stays in
the region. `position` is a corner or the middle of the top or bottom edge
(`bottom-end` by default; start and end follow the text direction); toasts
swipe away towards that side on touch. At most `max` (5) stay: a new toast
beyond that drops the oldest.

It renders into the overlay root only once mounted. The queue is one per
page; on the server `add` does nothing.

components.name: Toggle
components.purpose: A button that stays pressed or not, such as Bold in a text toolbar.
components.use: For an on-off choice shown as a button among other buttons (bold, mute, pin), where the press itself says the state.
components.avoid: For a setting with a label beside it, use Switch; for one choice among several buttons, use ToggleGroup; for an action, use Button.

adapts.input: On touch an md toggle is at least --weft-hit-min (44 px) tall, a small or square one through its hit area (Button's rule).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; it does not wrap.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Pressed or not, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Pressed at first when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: label
props.description: The text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the toggle is square and needs an `aria-label`.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: it posts `value` while pressed.

props.name: value
props.description: What a form post sends while pressed (default `on`).

props.name: id
props.description: The button's id.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour while not pressed.

props.name: variant
props.description: The variant while not pressed.

props.name: activeTone
props.description: The colour while pressed.

props.name: activeVariant
props.description: The variant while pressed.

props.name: square
props.description: Square, its width equal to its height.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (the change is being saved): a spinner, aria-busy, and no toggling.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Pressed or released.

components.notes:
Bind `v-model` to a boolean. It is a Button that says `aria-pressed`, so
assistive technology reads it as a toggle button (APG button pattern); a
press, Enter or Space changes it. Not pressed it is drawn with `variant`
and `tone` (`ghost`, `neutral`), pressed with `active-variant` and
`active-tone` (`soft`, `primary`). `label`, `icon`, `trailing-icon`,
`square`, `size` and the leading, default and trailing slots are Button's;
with only an icon give it an `aria-label`.

With a `name` it posts `value` (default `on`) with a plain form while
pressed, and nothing while not, as a checkbox does. `loading` (the change is
being saved) shows a spinner, says `aria-busy` and blocks every press;
`disabled` is the native attribute. In a FormField it takes the field's id
and disabled state.

It has no stylesheet of its own: it is drawn by Button's.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.purpose: A row of toggle buttons, one pressed or none, or any number with `multiple`.
components.use: For a small set of choices shown as buttons in a toolbar: text alignment, a view (list or grid), the styles of a selection.
components.avoid: For a choice in a form with labels, use RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup; for switching panels, use Tabs; for more than five or six options, use Select.

adapts.input: On touch every button is at least --weft-hit-min tall (Button's rule).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A horizontal group wraps onto more lines when its box is narrow (unless attached).

props.name: items
props.description: The buttons: `{ label, value, icon, trailingIcon, ariaLabel, disabled }`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The pressed value (null for none), or the pressed values with `multiple`, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: What is pressed when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Any number can be pressed.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (default) or `vertical`: which arrow keys move.

props.name: loop
props.description: The arrow keys wrap round at the ends.

props.name: attached
props.description: Join the buttons into one bar.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: each pressed value posts under it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the buttons not pressed.

props.name: variant
props.description: The variant of the buttons not pressed.

props.name: activeTone
props.description: The colour of the pressed buttons.

props.name: activeVariant
props.description: The variant of the pressed buttons.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every button is disabled.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The pressed value or values changed.

components.notes:
`items` are `{ label, value, icon, trailingIcon, ariaLabel, tone, variant,
disabled }` (a value defaults to the item's place). Bind `v-model` to the
pressed value (null for none), or, with `multiple`, to the list of pressed
values. Pressing the pressed item of a single group releases it.

It is a `role="group"` (give it an `aria-label`) of buttons that say
`aria-pressed`. **Keyboard:** the group is one tab stop, which rests on the
pressed item; the arrow keys move along it (Left and Right, mirrored right
to left; Up and Down when `orientation="vertical"`), wrapping round unless
`loop` is off; Home and End go to the ends; disabled items are passed by;
Enter and Space press.

`variant` and `tone` (`ghost`, `neutral`) draw the buttons not pressed,
`active-variant` and `active-tone` (`soft`, `primary`) the pressed ones.
`attached` joins them into one bar. With a `name` each pressed value posts
with a plain form. `disabled` disables every button. The default slot draws
a button's label (`{ item, index, pressed }`).

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: A short text about a control, shown on hover or keyboard focus.
components.use: For naming an icon button, or adding a short hint to a control, where hovering is how a pointer user would ask.
components.avoid: For anything a touch user needs, put it in the interface, since tooltips do not show on touch; for interactive content, use Popover.

adapts.input: On pointer it shows on hover after `delay` and at once on keyboard focus. On touch it renders nothing, and nothing hovers; a trigger with no name of its own is named by the text (aria-label), so the meaning stays.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It wraps at 20rem, and stays in view by flipping and sliding.

props.name: text
props.description: What it says. The content slot replaces it; give text anyway, as the name of a trigger that has none.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where it shows against the trigger: `top`, `bottom-start`, …

props.name: delay
props.description: ms of hover before it shows; focus shows it at once, and so does a hover just after another tooltip closed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Never shown.

props.name: open
props.description: Shown or hidden, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts shown when `v-model:open` is not bound.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Shown or hidden.

components.notes:
The default slot is the trigger, one element; `text` is what it says (the
`content` slot replaces it). It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern:
it never takes focus, and while shown the trigger is described by it
(`aria-describedby`, added after any description the trigger has).

It hides on Escape (only it, when it is the top overlay), on a press, when
the trigger loses focus, and when the pointer leaves both the trigger and the
tooltip, so the pointer can move onto it to read it. A press outside it
also goes on to the overlay below (a menu it shows over), so one press
closes both, while Escape closes only the tooltip. Once one tooltip has
hidden, the next shows without a delay for a moment, as when running the
pointer along a toolbar.

**Naming.** An icon-only trigger needs a name. When the trigger has none (no
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title` or text), the tooltip's text becomes
its `aria-label`, on pointer and touch alike, and the trigger is then not
described by it as well (it would be read twice). A trigger that has a name keeps
it; on touch the tooltip's extra hint is then not shown, so do not put what a
person must know in a tooltip.

`v-model:open` shows it from code; `disabled` never shows it.

components.name: Tree
components.purpose: A hierarchy of nodes that open and close, such as files in folders.
components.use: For a file browser, a table of contents, categories within categories.
components.avoid: For a flat list to choose from, use Listbox; for a site's links, NavigationMenu.

adapts.input: Each row is at least --weft-hit-min tall on touch (44 px rows when windowed).
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its container; labels are cut with an ellipsis.

props.name: items
props.description: The nodes at the top: `{ label, value, icon, children, defaultExpanded, disabled }`.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen node's key (null when none is), or the chosen keys with `multiple`, bound with `v-model`. A node's key is its `value`, else its labels from the top joined with `/`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The chosen node or nodes when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several nodes can be chosen.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Nodes can be chosen at all; false leaves only opening and closing (no aria-selected).

props.name: expanded
props.description: The keys of the open nodes, bound with `v-model:expanded`.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: The open nodes when `v-model:expanded` is not bound; default those marked `defaultExpanded`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be chosen, opened or closed.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The chosen node or nodes changed.

emits.name: update:expanded
emits.description: The open nodes changed.

emits.name: select
emits.description: A node was chosen (or, with `multiple`, toggled).

emits.name: toggle
emits.description: A node opened (true) or closed (false).

components.notes:
`items` are `{ label, value, icon, children, defaultExpanded, disabled }`.
A node's key is its `value`, else its labels from the top joined with `/`;
siblings with the same label and no value get `#2`, `#3`, … after it.
Bind the chosen node's key with `v-model` (`null` when none is; an array
with `multiple`), and the open nodes' keys with `v-model:expanded`.
`selectable: false` leaves only opening and closing. It emits `select` and
`toggle(item, open)`. The `item` slot replaces a node's label.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Tree View pattern, drawn as one flat list of
`treeitem`s that each state `aria-level`, `aria-setsize` and
`aria-posinset`, and `aria-expanded` when they have children; `aria-selected`
on every node while nodes can be chosen, and `aria-multiselectable` with
`multiple`. Name it with `aria-label`.

**Keyboard.** The tree is one tab stop. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move over the
visible nodes, Home and End to the first and last. ArrowRight opens a closed
node, or moves into an open one; ArrowLeft closes an open node, or moves to
its parent (both mirrored right to left). `*` opens every sibling of the
focused node. Typing jumps to a node by its label. Enter (or a press) chooses
the node and opens or closes it; Space chooses it. With `multiple`, Space
toggles a node, Shift with ArrowDown or ArrowUp moves and toggles, and
Ctrl+A chooses every visible node. Disabled nodes are reached but never
chosen, opened or closed.

**Long trees.** Past 200 visible nodes only the rows in view are rendered
(Weft's `useVirtualList`), each row a fixed height, and the tree scrolls
inside itself (`--weft-tree-height`, 20rem); the focused node is always
rendered.

components.name: WeftProvider
components.purpose: Sets how the part of the page inside it is used, its input and its surface, for every Weft component within.
components.use: Around a layout to declare its surface (landing for marketing pages, app for tools), and to force an input for a kiosk, a preview or a test.
components.avoid: For choosing a component's look, use its own props; never use it to make a mobile version of something, since components adapt themselves.

adapts.input: Left unset, it passes on the browser's detected input, pointer or touch, live (pointer until mounted, so a phone hydrates what the server drew); set, it overrides it for everything inside.
adapts.surface: Left unset, it passes on the outer one (app by default); set, it switches density, type scale and spacing for everything inside.
adapts.width: Nothing changes once mounted, since width comes from each component's own container; set, it is the width class drawn before anything is measured, on the server and while hydrating.

props.name: input
props.description: Force `pointer` or `touch` for everything inside; unset passes on the detected or outer input.

props.name: surface
props.description: `landing` or `app` density for everything inside; unset passes on the outer surface.

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale (`de-DE`, `ar-EG`) for dates and sizes inside: names, digits, the first day of the week; unset passes on the outer one.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; it has `display: contents`, so it does not affect layout.

props.name: inset
props.description: Everything inside is a preview of a page, drawn inside another (a gallery's stage or thumbnail): a Page or an AppShell in it draws no `<main>` landmark, a Page's title is an h2, and an AppShell keeps no collapsed state. An outer inset provider makes every one inside it inset too.

props.name: width
props.description: The width class to draw everything inside with before it can be measured: on the server and while hydrating (`narrow`, `regular` or `wide`); unset passes on the outer one, else `wide`. Once mounted, each component measures its own box. For a part of the page drawn at a known width, such as a picture of a phone.

components.notes:
Its element carries `data-weft-surface`, and `data-weft-input` when its
`input` is set, which the theme's CSS reads to switch control heights, hit
sizes and density. With no input set the theme follows `(pointer: coarse)`
at the root, so a page that is never hydrated still has 44 px targets on a
phone. Components read the detected input as `pointer` until they have
mounted, then switch live: the server cannot know it, and a phone hydrates
the pointer markup first. It renders
with `display: contents`, so it does not affect layout. Nested providers
override one axis and inherit the other.

`locale` (a BCP 47 tag, `de-DE`) sets the language of dates, times and sizes
for every component inside that has no `locale` of its own (Calendar,
DatePicker, DateRangePicker, InputTime, FileUpload): names, digits, the order
of day, month and year, the first day of the week. Unset, it passes on the
outer one; with none at all they use `en-US`, never the browser's language,
so the server renders what the browser hydrates.

`inset` says everything inside is a preview of a page, drawn inside another
(a gallery's stage or thumbnail, a screenshot frame): a Page or an AppShell
in it renders no `<main>` landmark, and a Page's title is an `h2`, so the
page around keeps one main and one h1. An AppShell in it keeps no collapsed
state in localStorage. An inset provider makes every one inside it inset too.

`width` (`narrow`, `regular` or `wide`) is the width class everything
inside is drawn with before it can be measured: on the server, and while
hydrating. Unset, it passes on the outer one, and with none at all
components start `wide`. Once mounted, each measures its own box and
follows it. Give it to a part drawn at a known width that is never
hydrated, such as a picture of a phone, so a Table in it is drawn as its
cards.
